mainTopic: Consecrating and redeeming fields: the wording of the משנה about כהנים and לוים, and the rules for bidding on a consecrated field when there is no יובל
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn from an extra letter in a פסוק that a field due to become ancestral is not treated like a bought field. Next the גמרא asks why the משנה says כהנים and לוים may always consecrate, since a ישראל may too. It answers that the wording simply matches the first משנה of the chapter, and that the real new point is about redeeming. The chapter אין מקדישין then ends. A new chapter teaches that when there is no יובל, the owner of a consecrated field opens the bidding, and the גמרא shows he can even be forced to. Several reasons support this: he loves the field, he has the first right to redeem, and he adds a חומש. The story of the man who bid an איסר (or an egg, according to רבי יוסי) turns out to be an argument about how small a redemption payment may be. A new משנה then rules that a bidder who backs out must cover the loss he causes הקדש, and that the owners win when their bid ties with an outsider's. The amud ends as an outsider bids twenty-one, and the ruling for that case comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The extra letter in the verse about a bought field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the source of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. The extra letter מ in 'מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ' teaches that only a field that will never become ancestral counts as a bought field.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, they found a verse and expounded it. The Torah could have written 'a field he bought, which is not his ancestral field,' or 'which is not an ancestral field.' Why does it say 'not of his ancestral field'? To teach: a field that is not due to become an ancestral field is treated as bought. This rules out a field that is due to become ancestral.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion by showing where רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn their view. Their view is that a son who bought his father's field and consecrated it before his father died still treats it as ancestral.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have been written more simply. The extra letter מ ('of') is therefore read as a limit. Only a field that can never become ancestral gets the rules of a שדה מקנה. A son's purchase from his father will one day become ancestral through inheritance, so it is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: A field someone bought, not inherited
An ancestral field that came down through the family
Fit or due to become something
To expound a verse and draw a law from its wording
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳

phrases.english: But here, they found a verse and expounded it:
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון from the discussion just before this.

'If a field that he bought,'
'which is not his ancestral field,'

steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון have no source for treating a field consecrated before the father's death as ancestral
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra letter מ excludes any field that is due to become ancestral from the rules of a bought field
steps.whatToRemember: A field that will one day become ancestral is not treated as a שדה מקנה. The source is the extra מ in 'מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ.'

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about כהנים and לוים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: כהנים and לוים may consecrate (and redeem) their fields at any time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהנים and the לוים may always consecrate, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full line in the משנה says כהנים and לוים may always consecrate and always redeem, both before and after the יובל. The 'וכו׳' points to the rest of that line, which the גמרא is about to discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: They consecrate, meaning they give the field to הקדש
Always, at any time
Levites, members of the tribe of לוי

phrases.english: The priests and the Levites
may always consecrate, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים and לוים may consecrate and redeem their ancestral fields at any time

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say כהנים may consecrate?
steps.stepSummary: Saying כהנים and לוים may always redeem makes sense, because a ישראל cannot. But a ישראל may also always consecrate, so why single out כהנים and לוים?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, 'they redeem' was needed. It rules out a ישראל, who may redeem only until the יובל, and teaches that כהנים and לוים may always redeem. But 'they consecrate': why mention כהנים and לוים specifically? Even a ישראל may do so too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts half of the משנה's line but questions the other half. It asks what new point 'they consecrate' adds for כהנים and לוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל who does not redeem his consecrated field before the יובל loses it to the כהנים. So 'כהנים redeem forever' is a real difference. Consecrating, though, is allowed for everyone at any time, so the word seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part makes sense
They redeem, meaning they buy the field back from הקדש
To exclude, to rule out
Why mention this case specifically?
The Jubilee, every fiftieth year

phrases.english: Granted, 'they redeem' was necessary,
to exclude the case of an Israelite,
who may redeem only until the Jubilee;
it teaches us
that priests and Levites may always redeem.
But 'they consecrate':
why specifically priests and Levites?
Even an Israelite may as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the quoted משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The word מקדישין in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Consecrating at any time is allowed for a ישראל too, so stating it for כהנים and לוים seems to teach nothing new
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether כהנים may consecrate. Everyone agrees they may. The question is why the משנה bothers to say it about them in particular.

steps.title: Maybe it means consecrating during the יובל year itself
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the משנה means כהנים and לוים may consecrate even during the יובל year itself. That works according to שמואל, who holds a ישראל's consecration in that year does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it means in the יובל year itself: this works for שמואל, who said that in the יובל year itself the field is not consecrated. Then the משנה teaches us that כהנים and לוים may always consecrate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer: 'always' includes the יובל year itself, when a ישראל cannot consecrate. The גמרא notes this works for שמואל's view, which sets up the problem with רב in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, a ישראל who consecrates his field during the יובל year achieves nothing. So saying כהנים and לוים can consecrate even then would be a real difference. The answer depends on שמואל's opinion, though.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible answer)
This works well for (a certain opinion)
During the יובל year itself
It does not become consecrated

phrases.english: And if you would say: during the Jubilee Year itself,
this works well for Shmuel, who said:
'In the Jubilee Year itself, it is not consecrated';
so it teaches us
that priests and Levites may always consecrate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the question on מקדישין
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to the יובל year itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Consecrate' seemed to teach nothing special about כהנים
steps.terutzMaskana: According to שמואל, it teaches that כהנים and לוים can consecrate even during the יובל year, when a ישראל cannot

steps.title: The answer fails according to רב
steps.stepSummary: According to רב, a ישראל can also consecrate during the יובל year. So for him the question returns: why single out כהנים and לוים?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב, why mention כהנים and לוים specifically? Even a ישראל may do so too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the answer from the last step does not work for everyone. According to רב, the original question comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that a ישראל's consecration during the יובל year does take effect. So the 'יובל year itself' answer creates no difference between כהנים and a ישראל. For רב, the word 'consecrate' still seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: But according to (another opinion)

phrases.english: But according to Rav,
why specifically priests and Levites?
Even an Israelite may as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַב, מַאי אִירְיָא כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proposed answer according to רב
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The answer works only for שמואל, not for רב
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רב, a ישראל can also consecrate during the יובל year, so there is no difference

steps.title: By your logic, 'before and after the יובל' is also extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question around. The משנה also says 'both before and after the יובל,' which adds nothing after 'always.' So not every phrase in this משנה is there to teach something new.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, why do I need 'both before the יובל and after the יובל'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the questioner by pointing to another phrase in the same משנה that is also extra. This prepares the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the משנה says 'always,' adding 'before and after the יובל' repeats the same idea. If that phrase can be extra, the word 'consecrate' can be extra too. The challenge weakens the original question rather than answering it directly.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turning the logic back on the questioner)
Why do I need this?

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
'both before the Jubilee'
'and after the Jubilee': why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the questioner's own logic against him
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that every phrase in the משנה must teach something new
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Before and after the יובל' clearly adds nothing after 'always,' so the משנה does include extra wording
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new attack on the משנה. The גמרא is defending it by showing the original question asked too much.

steps.title: The wording matches the earlier משנה
steps.stepSummary: The first משנה of the chapter mentioned 'before the יובל' and 'after the יובל.' So this later משנה repeated that wording to match, even though nothing new is taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since the first משנה taught 'before the יובל and after the יובל,' the later משנה also taught 'both after the יובל and before the יובל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the extra phrase is there only to match the wording of the earlier משנה. In the same way, the word 'consecrate' does not need to teach something special about כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first משנה of this chapter (24a) set time limits for a ישראל. He may not consecrate shortly before the יובל, and may not redeem shortly after it. The later משנה echoes those words for כהנים and לוים to show the contrast, even where there is no new law. This shows that a משנה sometimes includes words just to keep its style parallel.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because of (wording carried along from another place)
The first part; here, the earlier משנה
The latter part; here, the later משנה

phrases.english: Rather, since the first part taught
phrases.notes: That's the first משנה of the chapter, on 24a, about a ישראל's field.

phrases.english: 'before the Jubilee and after the Jubilee,'
the latter part also taught
'both after the Jubilee and before the Jubilee.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the extra wording raised in the previous step
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel wording carried over from an earlier משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every phrase in the משנה must teach something new
steps.terutzMaskana: Some wording appears just to match the earlier משנה, so the question 'why mention consecrating' loses its force
steps.whatToRemember: A משנה sometimes repeats wording to match an earlier משנה, even with no new law. This is called 'אַיְּידֵי.'

steps.title: The words 'consecrate and redeem' were also repeated to match the first משנה
steps.stepSummary: The answer from step 7 is stretched further. Since the first משנה said ישראלים 'may not consecrate and may not redeem,' the later משנה said כהנים and לוים 'may consecrate and redeem,' even though the word 'consecrate' teaches nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the first משנה said 'they may not consecrate and may not redeem,' the later משנה also said 'they may consecrate and redeem.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same idea from step 7 to explain why the משנה mentions consecrating for כהנים and לוים at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original question (step 3) was: why does the משנה say כהנים and לוים may consecrate, if a ישראל may too? Now the answer is that the word 'consecrate' is only there to match the wording of the first משנה, which mentioned both consecrating and redeeming. The real new point is about redeeming.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he already taught. This means the wording was copied to match, not to teach something new.
The first part, here meaning the earlier משנה.
The later part, here meaning the later משנה.
They redeem (buy the field back from הקדש).

steps.whatToRemember: The question 'why mention consecrating?' is answered: the משנה just matched the wording of the first משנה. The real new teaching for כהנים and לוים is that they may always redeem.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common tool of the גמרא: sometimes a משנה repeats words only so its style matches an earlier משנה. Not every word has to teach a new law.

phrases.english: And since he taught in the first part
"they may not consecrate and may not redeem,"
he also taught in the latter part
"they may consecrate and redeem."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the step 7 answer (matching the earlier wording) to finally resolve the step 3 question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic matching: the word is there to mirror the earlier משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every phrase in the משנה must teach something new, so 'consecrate' must have a special meaning for כהנים and לוים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Consecrate' was only repeated to match the first משנה. The new point is about redeeming.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter אין מקדישין
steps.stepSummary: The chapter אין מקדישין ends with the traditional closing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter אין מקדישין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the chapter, said when finishing a פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks that the discussion of this chapter is complete and a new chapter begins next.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the line said when finishing a chapter.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
chapter "They may not consecrate."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final answer in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter אין מקדישין is complete.

steps.title: With no יובל, the owner is asked to open the bidding
steps.stepSummary: A new chapter opens. If someone consecrates his field at a time when the יובל is not in effect, the treasurer tells him to bid first, because the owner pays an extra fifth and others do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who consecrates his field at a time when there is no יובל: the treasurer says to him, 'You open the bidding first,' because the owner adds a חומש, and no one else adds a חומש.
steps.whatsHappening: The new משנה gives a rule for selling a consecrated field when there is no יובל: the owner is asked to make the first bid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no יובל, the field is not redeemed at the fixed price from the תורה. Instead it is sold by bidding, based on its value. The owner must add a חומש on top of his bid, so letting him bid first brings more money to הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (here shortened to מַתְנִי׳).
One who consecrates (gives something to the Temple treasury).
The Jubilee year, every fiftieth year.
An extra fifth that the owner adds when he redeems his own consecrated item.
The owners. Here it means the person who consecrated the field.

steps.confusionAlert: The 'he' who speaks is the Temple treasurer, and 'him' is the owner. 'Says to him' sounds like a polite request, but the גמרא in steps 14–16 shows that in the end the owner can be forced to open the bidding.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who consecrates his field
at a time when there is no Jubilee,
he says to him: "You open first,"
phrases.notes: The treasurer is speaking to the owner, inviting him to make the first bid.

phrases.english: because the owners give a fifth,
and every other person does not give a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֶת שָׂדֵהוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאֵין הַיּוֹבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When there is no יובל, the owner of a consecrated field is asked to open the bidding, since he adds a חומש.

steps.title: A man consecrates a bad field and bids one איסר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells of a man who consecrated a poor field. When asked to bid first, he offered only an איסר, a tiny coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case of a man who consecrated his field because it was poor. They told him, 'You open first.' He said, 'It is mine for an איסר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts a story that shows the bidding rule in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The field was poor, so no one else wanted it. The owner was asked to bid first, and he offered almost nothing: a single איסר.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a true story brought to teach a law.
Its poor quality (the field was bad).
A small coin of very little value.

phrases.english: There was an incident with one who consecrated his field
because of its poor quality,
they said to him: You open first.
He said: It is hereby mine for an issar.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁהִקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ מִפְּנֵי רָעָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rule from step 10 in a real story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner who opened the bidding offered just one איסר for his poor field.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: he bid an egg, not an איסר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the man really bid an egg, because הקדש can be redeemed with money or with something worth money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: He did not say 'for an איסר' but 'for an egg,' because הקדש can be redeemed with money or with something worth money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי breaks into the story to correct one detail: what the man actually offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says the bid was even smaller, an egg, which is worth less than an איסר. He explains that this is allowed, since הקדש may be redeemed with an item that is worth money, not only with coins.

keyTerms.meaning: An egg, worth even less than an איסר.
Consecrated property belonging to the Temple.
Is redeemed (bought back).
Something worth money, an item instead of coins.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לֹא אָמַר זֶה ״בְּאִיסָּר״,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: This man did not say "for an issar,"
rather, "for an egg,"
because consecrated property is redeemed with money and with money's worth,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לֹא אָמַר זֶה ״בְּאִיסָּר״, אֶלָּא ״בְּבֵיצָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the detail of the story told in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrated property may be redeemed with something worth money, such as an egg.

steps.title: The treasurer accepts, and the man gets his field back almost free
steps.stepSummary: The treasurer told the man the field was his. In the end, he lost only an איסר and got his field back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The treasurer said to him, 'It is yours.' So he lost only an איסר, and his field was back in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: the low bid was accepted, and the owner got his field back for almost nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The treasurer accepted the owner's tiny bid, so the field was his again. The story shows that when the owner opens the bidding, his offer can be accepted even if it is very low.

keyTerms.meaning: It has reached you. In other words, the field is now yours.
Loses.

steps.whatToRemember: When there is no יובל, a consecrated field is sold by bidding, and the owner bids first because he adds a חומש. In the story, the owner's tiny bid was accepted, so he lost almost nothing.

phrases.english: He said to him: "It has come to you,"
phrases.notes: This is the treasurer accepting the bid and telling him the field is his.

phrases.english: it turns out he loses an issar
and his field is before him.
phrases.notes: He means the field is back in the man's hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: ״הִגַּעְתִּיךָ״, נִמְצָא מַפְסִיד אִיסָּר וְשָׂדֵהוּ לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story from step 11, after רבי יוסי's side comment in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The owner's tiny opening bid was accepted, so he got his poor field back at almost no cost.

steps.title: Does the treasurer tell the owner, or force him?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the treasurer 'tells' the owner to bid first, but a ברייתא says the owner is 'forced' to bid first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: One who consecrates his field at a time when the יובל is not in effect, they tell him to bid first. Is it really just 'telling'? But a ברייתא teaches that they force him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the משנה. It points out that the משנה's wording ('they tell him') clashes with a ברייתא that says 'they force him.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Telling' sounds like a polite request the owner may refuse. 'Forcing' means he has no choice. Both sources describe the same case, so the גמרא needs to explain the gap.

keyTerms.meaning: They say / they tell him: a request
They force him: a requirement
One who consecrates his field to הקדש

phrases.english: GEMARA: One who consecrates his field at a time, etc.
They 'say' to him? But it was taught in a ברייתא: they force him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in Steps 10-13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא uses the stronger word כופין for the same case, which suggests the owner is required, not just asked.

steps.title: 'Telling' really means forcing
steps.stepSummary: The word 'tell' in the משנה also means 'force.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'they tell him' mean? It also means they force him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sources mean the same thing. The משנה's 'tell' is a strong instruction, which is forcing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer reads the משנה's softer word in light of the ברייתא. There is no argument between the sources, only different wording.

keyTerms.meaning: What does ... mean? It also means ...: a way of reading one word as matching another

phrases.english: What does 'they say' mean? It also means they force.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אומרין means a polite request the owner can refuse.
steps.terutzMaskana: אומרין itself means forcing, the same as the ברייתא.

steps.title: First they ask, then they force
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: first they ask the owner; if he obeys, fine, and if not, they force him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: At first they ask him. If he listens, he listens. If not, they force him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to settle the clash. The משנה and the ברייתא describe two stages of the same process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'tell' keeps its soft meaning. The משנה describes the first step, a request. The ברייתא describes what happens if the owner refuses, which is forcing.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces a second answer
At first, at the beginning
He listens / obeys

steps.whatToRemember: Either way, the owner ends up having to bid first. The two answers only differ on whether he is asked nicely before being forced.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: at first they tell him,
if he listens, he listens,
and if not, they force him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of Step 14, different from Step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא disagree about whether the owner is forced.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה describes the first request, and the ברייתא describes the forcing that follows if he refuses.

steps.title: Why does the משנה give the חומש as the reason?
steps.stepSummary: Why does the משנה say the owner bids first because he pays a חומש? There are other reasons: he loves his field, and the Torah gives him the first right to redeem.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: Because the owner gives an extra fifth, etc. Why give specifically this reason? It should give the reason that the field is dear to him, so he will bid higher and redeem it. And also, the מצוה of redeeming belongs first to the owner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the reason the משנה gives for why the owner bids first. It offers two other reasons that seem more basic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says it is because the owner adds a חומש, so הקדש earns more. The גמרא says there are stronger reasons. The owner loves his field and will bid high, and the Torah gives the owner the first right to redeem.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? Why pick this reason?
Let him get it from: there is a better source or reason
An extra fifth the owner adds when he redeems his own consecrated item
It is dear to him
The מצוה of redeeming belongs first to the owner

phrases.english: Because the owner gives an extra fifth, etc.
Why specifically because the owner gives a fifth?
Let him get it from a different reason:
that since the field is dear to him,
he will add more and redeem it!
And furthermore, the מצוה of redemption is with the owner!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה, the reason given for the owner bidding first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's reason: שהבעלים נותנין חומש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two more basic reasons exist, the owner's love for the field and the owner's first right to redeem, so why mention only the חומש?

steps.title: All three reasons are true
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means one reason and then more: the owner's love for the field, his first right to redeem, and the חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is saying one reason and more. One: since the field is dear to him, he will add more and redeem it. Another: the מצוה of redeeming belongs to the owner. And another: the owner gives an extra fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה does not reject the other reasons. They are all true, and the חומש is added on top of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads the משנה as building a list. The first two reasons are understood, and the משנה states the extra one, the חומש. Nothing in the question is wrong; the משנה just did not spell everything out.

keyTerms.meaning: It says one reason, and another: there are several reasons together
He redeems

steps.whatToRemember: The owner bids first for three reasons together: he loves the field, the Torah gives him first right to redeem, and he adds a חומש.

phrases.english: It is saying one reason, and another:
One: that since it is dear to him,
he will add more and redeem it;
and another: the מצוה of redemption is with the owner;
and another: that the owner gives a fifth, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה gives the חומש as its only reason, ignoring the others.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה accepts the other two reasons and adds the חומש as a further reason.

steps.title: Is the argument about whether something worth money counts as money?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוסי holds that something worth money counts as money, while the רבנן hold it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: There was a story with a man who consecrated his field, etc. Shall we say this is what they argue about? רבי יוסי holds that something worth money is like money, and the רבנן hold that something worth money is not like money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the story from Steps 11-13 and suggests what the argument is about. This is a proposal that the גמרא will test next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said the man bid an איסר, a coin. רבי יוסי said he bid an egg, an item worth money. The suggestion is that they differ on whether an item worth money can be used to redeem הקדש like real money.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? A suggestion the גמרא may later reject
They argue / disagree
Something worth money is treated like money

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a suggestion (לימא). Do not take it as the final explanation of the argument; the גמרא will challenge it next.

phrases.english: There was an incident with one who consecrated his field, etc.
Shall we say that they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף כְּכֶסֶף,
phrases.english: that רבי יוסי holds something worth money is like money,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף אֵינוֹ כְּכֶסֶף.
phrases.english: and the רבנן hold something worth money is not like money.
phrases.notes: The רבנן here are the first opinion in the משנה, who said the man bid an איסר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the story in the משנה and proposes the basis of the argument between רבי יוסי and the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the underlying disagreement between the רבנן (איסר) and רבי יוסי (egg)?

steps.title: But everyone holds that something worth money counts as money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges its own suggestion from Step 19. It is an accepted rule that שווה כסף ככסף, so how could the רבנן disagree?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we have an established rule that something worth money is treated like money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion it just made. It reminds us of a known rule: something worth money counts as money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the רבנן hold that something worth money is NOT like money. But שווה כסף ככסף is an accepted rule. If the suggestion were right, the רבנן would be going against a known law, so the suggestion cannot stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Something worth money is treated like money (it can be used to pay or redeem)
It is established for us; an accepted rule

phrases.english: But it is established for us
that something worth money is like money!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion in Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the רבנן reject the rule שווה כסף ככסף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שווה כסף ככסף is an accepted rule, so the רבנן cannot be disagreeing with it.

steps.title: They actually argue about an item whose fifth is worth less than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that שווה כסף ככסף. The dispute is whether we can redeem with something so small that its חומש is not worth a פרוטה. The תנא קמא allows an איסר but not less. רבי יוסי allows even an item worth an egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees that something worth money is like money. Here they argue about redeeming with something whose fifth is not worth a פרוטה. The first opinion holds that with an איסר, whose fifth is worth a פרוטה, we redeem. רבי יוסי holds that we redeem even with something worth an egg.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by moving the argument to a new point. Both sides accept שווה כסף ככסף. They argue about how small the redemption payment is allowed to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner must add a חומש when he redeems. The תנא קמא says the payment must be big enough that its fifth is at least a פרוטה, and an איסר works because its fifth is more than a פרוטה. רבי יוסי says even something worth only an egg works, even though its fifth is worth less than a פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Its fifth; the extra fifth the owner adds when he redeems
The smallest coin that has legal value
A small coin worth eight פרוטות
The first, unnamed opinion; here, the רבנן

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that something worth money is like money. The argument is only about how small the payment may be: the רבנן want a fifth worth at least a פרוטה, and רבי יוסי allows even an egg's worth.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase כְּבֵיצָה here does not mean an egg-sized volume, the way it often does in טומאה. It means an item worth about as much as an egg.

phrases.english: Everyone agrees
that something worth money is like money,
and here they argue about redeeming with an item
whose fifth is not worth a פרוטה.
The first תנא holds: an איסר,
whose fifth is worth a פרוטה, we redeem with,
phrases.notes: An איסר is eight פרוטות, so its fifth is more than one פרוטה.

phrases.english: and רבי יוסי holds: with something worth an egg we also redeem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the dispute to a different point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sides argue about whether שווה כסף ככסף
steps.terutzMaskana: Both accept שווה כסף ככסף. They argue whether we may redeem with an item whose חומש is less than a פרוטה.

steps.title: The unattributed line in the משנה follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of the מעשה in the משנה: the treasurer said 'it has come to you,' so the owner lost only an איסר and kept his field. Because this line says איסר and not an egg, it follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'It has come to you.' So it turns out he lost only an איסר and his field stayed with him. This unattributed statement follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ending of the מעשה from the משנה. It points out that this unnamed line matches the view of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's ending says the owner lost an איסר. That fits the רבנן's version of the story, in which the owner bid an איסר. According to רבי יוסי he bid only an egg's worth, so this line is not his view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It has come to you'; the field is now yours at your bid
It turns out he loses
An unattributed statement, with no sage's name attached
The Sages; here, the תנא קמא

steps.whatToRemember: The line 'he lost an איסר' follows the רבנן, because it matches their view that the payment was an איסר.

phrases.english: He said to him: 'It has come to you,'
phrases.notes: The treasurer is telling the owner that his low bid is accepted.

phrases.english: so it turns out he loses an איסר
and his field is before him.
This unattributed line follows the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the explanation in Step 21 to identify whose view the end of the משנה follows
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ending of the מעשה, where the owner loses an איסר, follows the רבנן.

steps.title: New משנה: five people bid more and more on the field
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה describes five bidders on a הקדש field: ten סלעים, then twenty, thirty, forty and fifty.
steps.simpleTranslation: One person said: 'It is mine for ten סלעים.' Another said: 'For twenty.' Another said: 'For thirty.' Another said: 'For forty.' Another said: 'For fifty.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets up a case where several people keep raising their bids on a הקדש field, which prepares for the rules that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person bids ten סלעים more than the one before. This ladder of bids is the background for the question of what happens when the highest bidders back out.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Sela coins, a standard silver coin
'It is hereby mine'; the wording of a bid

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אֶחָד: ״הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁלִּי בְּעֶשֶׂר סְלָעִים״,
phrases.english: One said: 'It is hereby mine for ten סלעים,'
and one says: 'For twenty,'
and one says: 'For thirty,'
and one says: 'For forty,'
and one says: 'For fifty.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אֶחָד: הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁלִּי בְּעֶשֶׂר סְלָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a case of five rising bids on a הקדש field.

steps.title: Each bidder who backs out pays the difference he caused
steps.stepSummary: When the fifty, forty, thirty or twenty bidder backs out, the treasurer takes collateral from his property for ten סלעים, the gap between his bid and the next one down. If the ten bidder backs out, the field is sold at its value and he pays whatever is missing up to ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the fifty bidder backed out, they take collateral from his property for up to ten. If the forty bidder backed out, they take from his property up to ten. If the thirty bidder backed out, they take from his property up to ten. If the twenty bidder backed out, they take from his property up to ten. If the ten bidder backed out, they sell the field at its value and collect the remainder from the ten bidder.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules on what happens when the bidders back out one by one. Each one must make up the loss his backing out caused הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the top bidder backs out, the field goes to the next bidder down, who offered ten less. So the one who backed out pays that ten, and הקדש still gets the higher amount. When the last bidder, at ten, backs out, the field is sold for whatever it is worth, and he pays the gap between that price and his bid of ten.

keyTerms.meaning: He backed out of his offer
They take collateral; they seize property to collect
At its actual value
They collect payment
The remainder; the missing difference

steps.whatToRemember: Someone who bids on הקדש and backs out must pay whatever loss his backing out caused, so הקדש never loses money.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Up to ten' does not mean each person pays the whole amount he bid. He pays only the ten-סלע gap between his bid and the next bid below it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a bid to הקדש is binding: a promise to הקדש works like a real obligation, and the bidder answers for any loss he causes.

phrases.english: If the one of fifty backed out,
they take collateral from his property up to ten.
phrases.notes: The field now goes to the forty bidder, so the fifty bidder covers the missing ten.

phrases.english: If the one of forty backed out,
they take collateral from his property up to ten.
If the one of thirty backed out,
they take collateral from his property up to ten,
if the one of twenty backed out,
they take collateral from his property up to ten,
if the one of ten backed out,
they sell it at its value,
and collect the remainder from the one of ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר בּוֹ שֶׁל חֲמִשִּׁים מְמַשְׁכְּנִין מִנְּכָסָיו עַד עֶשֶׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the rulings for the bidding case set up in Step 23
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bidder who backs out pays the difference between his bid and the next lower bid. If the lowest bidder backs out, the field is sold at its value and he pays the shortfall.

steps.title: Equal bids: the owners come first
steps.stepSummary: If the owners and an outsider both bid twenty, the owners win the field, because they have to add a חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owners say 'twenty' and anyone else also says 'twenty,' the owners come first, because they add a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule for the הקדש auction. When the original owners and an outsider offer the same amount, the owners get the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An owner who redeems his own הקדש must pay an extra חומש, but an outsider does not. So an owner's bid of twenty really brings in more money for הקדש than an outsider's bid of twenty. Since הקדש gains more, the owners are given priority.

keyTerms.meaning: The owners, meaning the person who gave the field to הקדש
Come first, have priority
They add a fifth on top of the price
Any other person, an outsider

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the guiding idea of the whole auction: הקדש should always end up with the most money.

phrases.english: If the owners say: for twenty,
and any other person says: for twenty —
the owners come first,
because they add a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבְּעָלִים אוֹמְרִים בְּעֶשְׂרִים, וְכׇל אָדָם אוֹמְרִים בְּעֶשְׂרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה about the הקדש auction with a new case: equal bids from the owner and an outsider.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the owners and an outsider bid the same, the owners have priority because they add a חומש.

steps.title: An outsider raises the bid to twenty-one
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts a new case: an outsider says he will take the field for twenty-one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one person said: 'It is mine for twenty-one' —
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up its next case. An outsider bids one סלע more than the owners, and the ruling for this case comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the outsider's bid is higher than the owners' bid of twenty. The question is whether the outsider wins, or whether the owners can still win once we count their חומש. The משנה has only given the setup so far, and the answer is still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, it is mine, the wording a bidder uses to take on the field at his price

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished. The ruling for the bid of twenty-one is given in the next lines of the משנה, so do not read this line as a complete rule.

phrases.english: If one person said:
phrases.notes: He means an outsider, not one of the owners.

phrases.english: "It is mine for twenty-one" —

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אֶחָד: הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁלִּי בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְאַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the equal-bid case by having the outsider raise his bid by one סלע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of an outsider bidding twenty-one against the owners' twenty. The ruling follows in the next part of the משנה.
